decisions.evidence: Both component revisions are leaked transcription prompts, not voice-line text; the filename expects a Dynamo roof ping.
Wall and walls are both grammatical and the adjacent Oathkeeper scene does not establish the spoken number.
Totten is the conventional surname spelling and Toten appears phonetic, but no repository vocabulary entry independently names Frederick.
The revisions differ in spoken conjunctions as well as punctuation; both lists are grammatical.
You are versus you're is a recording-level contraction difference; the later official Baxter Society line is separate dialogue.
Doesn't versus does not cannot be inferred; the later Hidden King wording is a distinct patron-era transcript.
Queen & Coven is plausibly the bestseller's styled title, while later generic queen and coven uses remain lowercase; no authoritative title list confirms it.
The canonical pocket/pocket_select_04 parallel uses Today's across two other hashes, but these synth hashes may be distinct recordings.
OSIC Sandman matches local Sandman Division terminology, while OSIC's Sandman is also plausible for Haze; the possessive sound requires audio evidence.
There's versus there is is a contraction difference; punctuation alone cannot prove the recording.
Scream versus screaming, in frustration versus frustration, and ol' versus old are spoken semantic differences among four plausible variants.
Trooper and troopers are both grammatical and the filename does not establish singular or plural.
Rule versus ruled and the presence of uh are spoken tense/filler differences that grammar cannot settle.
It is versus it's is an unsupported contraction choice; both component revisions are otherwise grammatical.
I prefer and I'd prefer differ in spoken modality and are both natural Wraith lines.
Free and freed are both grammatical but encode different tense; no parallel line resolves the recording.
The later official line independently begins You've proven, favoring revision 2, but its Hidden King ending is separate era-specific dialogue.
Shadowlands and Shadowline are prototype game-term variants; the repository also preserves Neon Prime and Deadlock versions of this tutorial line.
This day is versus this day's is a spoken contraction/wording difference, and both sentences are grammatical.
There is versus there's and enemy's shrine versus enemy shrine are recording-level wording differences.
Anyway and anyways are both possible spoken forms; punctuation does not establish the final s.
Cindermaw and legal-style v. are more plausible than Cindermar and vs., but no authoritative repository vocabulary confirms the fictional case name.
Revision 2 is the only fully grammatical account of Lash's boast, but filler placement and exact wording remain recording-dependent.
You're versus you are is a contraction difference; both correctly use the authoritative Paradox name.
Beef/bee and our/her are semantic differences, and none is clearly supported by the Chrono filename or nearby repository lines.
Rime and Riven are apparent prototype character-name variants, while the later official Grey Talon/Archmother line is separate final-era material.
The parallel high-streak file says Sandy can't be allowed to complete the ritual; can reverses the intended enemy warning.
I've got versus I got and getting versus gettin' are contraction/register differences across plausible recordings.
Both generated options are syntactically suspect and differ in tense; the likely sentence cannot be reconstructed by selecting either confidently.
OSIC is the authoritative organization acronym used throughout Haze and Dynamo lines; OSI is a truncation.
The filename and authoritative character name identify Lash; lass conflicts with the masculine self-reference and character identity.
Flying in on someone is the only grammatical ability-related phrase; revision 0 omits in and revision 1 is nonsensical.
Chrono maps authoritatively to Paradox, and singular Paradox fits the direct address; Paradoxs is malformed.
Soul and souls are both grammatical, meaningful number differences; neither the idol-drop filename nor parallels resolve them.
Enemy objectives and an enemy objective are both valid tutorial claims with different number and article.
LaPree is the more conventional spelling and preserves the apparent French surname form, but repository vocabulary does not name this expert.
We are versus we're is solely an unsupported contraction choice.
Fist and fists are both grammatical and the power-up filename does not prove the spoken number.
Extra coins and an extra coin are different valid reward descriptions; grammar cannot determine the game-era wording.
The filename, character mapping, and vocabulary all require Haze; Caze is a generation error.
Parallel Oathkeeper scene files explicitly say Gen? and Gen Geist, establishing the character spelling Gen rather than Jen.
History's versus history is is an exact spoken contraction distinction repeated twice; both are grammatical.
McGinnis can deploy one or multiple turrets, so turret and turrets are both plausible number choices; the official replacement is different dialogue.
Numerous parallel lines address Viscous with the singular nickname Biscuit; Biscuits is unsupported.
We are versus we're is a contraction difference with no recording-specific evidence.
Is versus apostrophe-s is a spoken contraction difference; both sentences fit the Bebop laser filename.
Played her part to perfection is the fixed idiom and matches the Paradox Rejuvenator-steal filename; parts is erroneous.
The filename describes Haze seeing Lash's massive entrance, making the compliment You know how to make an entrance, Lash the coherent named-character line.
They're versus they are is an unsupported contraction choice; both otherwise match the ability line.
Fine versus it's fine is a spoken filler/subject difference; both remaining variants are coherent Lash dialogue.
Called and call are distinct valid tenses; repository evidence establishes Fathom but not the recording's tense.
Guardian at the end and Guardian that's at the end are both grammatical and differ by spoken words.
Revision 0 correctly uses Oracle's and standard off-Broadway styling, and Gray Coven is plausible; no independent source confirms Gray versus Great.
Revision 0 is clearly corrupt, but give me and gimme are both possible spoken forms in the two coherent revisions.
Dorman is misspelled and lowercase doorman loses the authoritative character-name capitalization, so neither existing revision is clearly correct.
Repository material presents Cadence as the Ixian singer and revision 0's she is likely, but no direct same-line parallel proves the pronoun.
Best friend and best friends are both grammatical and may reflect a different number of summoned familiars or recordings.
Something versus somethin' is a pronunciation/transcription-register difference not resolvable from grammar.
A parallel patron introduction explicitly says I am Ambition Spark, establishing the proper patron name and spacing.
Transit line and Shadowline are distinct game-era terms, while a/the final push also differs; these hashes may represent evolved tutorial recordings.
